concerns.text: Task T012-Calc (Power Analysis) is marked as [P] (parallel-safe) but has a strict sequential dependency on T012.0 (Effect Size Doc) and T060 (Scope Boundary). The [P] tag is incorrect as these tasks cannot run in parallel; T012-Calc consumes the artifact produced by T012.0.

Task T012-Runtime (Power Gate) is marked as [P] but depends on T012-Calc. The [P] tag implies it can run in parallel with T012-Calc, which is impossible as it validates the output of T012-Calc. This violates the 'Producer before consumer' rule.

Task T093 (Document Ladder of Explanation) depends on T081, but T081 is marked [X] (completed) in Phase 6. However, T093 is listed in Phase 6.2 with a dependency on T081 which is in Phase 6. The ordering is semantically valid (Phase 6 before 6.2), but T093 is marked [ ] (unstarted) while T081 is [X]. If T081 is truly complete, T093 should be executable. However, T093 is blocked by T060 and T081. The real issue is T093 is marked [ ] but T090/T091/T092 in Phase 6.1 are marked [X] (superseded). The dependency chain T093 -> T081 -> T060 is valid, but the presence of superseded tasks (T090-T092) creates confusion about the active dependency path. More critically, T093 depends on T081, but T081 is in Phase 6, and T093 is in Phase 6.2. This is valid ordering, but the [P] tag on T093 (if it had one) would be wrong. Wait, T093 does not have [P]. The issue is T093 depends on T081, but T081 is marked [X] (completed) in the text, yet T093 is [ ]. This is a state inconsistency, not strictly ordering. Let's look for a harder ordering violation. T035 (ANOVA) depends on T038, T012-Runtime, T017, T027.3, T035.1. T035.1 depends on T027.3. T027.3 depends on T027.2. T027.2 depends on T017, T027.1, T006.3-Filter. T017 depends on T006.3-Filter. T006.3-Filter depends on T006.2-Calc. T006.2-Calc depends on T006.1-LoadSubset. This chain is valid. However, T035 depends on T012-Runtime. T012-Runtime depends on T012-Calc. T012-Calc depends on T012.0. T012.0 depends on T060. T060 is in Phase 2. T035 is in Phase 5. This is valid. The critical violation is the [P] tags on sequential tasks in Phase 2.
